summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fevers, lethargy, and a productive cough after a recent clinic visit, where he was found to have a urinary tract infection. He has a complex history including multiple myeloma, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, and a neobladder from prior bladder cancer. Admission labs showed acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 1.4, likely due to dehydration, and a urinalysis with high white blood cells. Urine culture confirmed VRE, and he was treated with IV daptomycin, later transitioned to oral linezolid. He developed oral ulcers during admission, managed with acyclovir. His renal function improved with IV fluids, and he received a transfusion for anemia. INR remained subtherapeutic but stable, so warfarin was continued without dose change. He remained afebrile, with resolving symptoms, and was discharged home on antibiotics and adjusted medications with close follow-up planned.
